_why: Skill-candidates row `run every published expect 0 screen at the freeze sha before certifying "no census moved"` (#49w), plus the fresh-context review of 5cba8c6b. h_mad_expect_screens.py reads each document from the working tree, finds every statement in a bash/sh fence ending `# expect <N>` (quote-, comment- and heredoc-aware boundaries), runs each qualifying block once in a throwaway detached worktree AT the sha with stdin from /dev/null and repository-redirecting GIT_* variables dropped, captures each screen's stdout between markers, and refuses (UNREADABLE, never PASS) a died, repeated or mangled screen, a pipeline member exiting >=2, an earlier recorded failure, or non-integer output. The worktree is removed on every path including SIGTERM, deleting only its own entry. No screen at all is NONE (exit 3), not PASS. Each row breaks one of those properties.

mutations.name: backslash-continuation-ignored
mutations._mechanism: A statement continued by a trailing backslash is split: the begin marker lands inside it.

mutations.name: operator-continuation-ignored
mutations._mechanism: A statement continued by a trailing `|` is split: `cmd | printf <marker>`.

mutations.name: operator-read-past-the-comment
mutations._mechanism: Review M1: `cmd |   # note` is judged by its raw text, so the pipe is missed and the tagged command reads stdin.

mutations.name: blank-line-ends-the-pipe
mutations._mechanism: Review M1: a blank line after `cmd |` is taken as the end of the statement.

mutations.name: quoted-continuation-ignored
mutations._mechanism: A line that starts inside a multi-line quoted string is taken as a statement start; the marker lands inside the string.
mutations.find: if lines[start].quoted or lines[start].body is not None:  # M:CONT-QUOTED

mutations.name: heredoc-terminator-ends-the-pipe
mutations._mechanism: Review S1: `cat <<X |` ... `X` is judged at the terminator line, so the pipe into the next line is missed.
mutations.find: k = lines[j].body if lines[j].body is not None else j

mutations.name: heredoc-body-tagged
mutations._mechanism: Review S1: a `# expect` line inside a heredoc body is a screen; its markers are written into the heredoc's file.
mutations.find: continue  # M:HEREDOC-BODY: a body line has no code and no comment
mutations.replace: pass  # M:HEREDOC-BODY: a body line has no code and no comment

mutations.name: heredoc-end-not-extended
mutations._mechanism: Review S1: a screen that opens a heredoc ends at its own line; the end marker goes into the body.
mutations.find: end = info.heredoc_end if info.heredoc_end is not None else i  # M:HEREDOC-END

mutations.name: screen-matched-anywhere-in-the-line
mutations._mechanism: Review N3: `# expect` inside a quoted string is taken as a screen.

mutations.name: double-quotes-not-tracked
mutations._mechanism: Review N3: a `#` inside double quotes starts a comment.

mutations.name: non-shell-fence-run
mutations._mechanism: A python (or any) fence is treated as shell, so its `# expect` comments become screens.
mutations.find: body = [] if words and words[0] in ("bash", "sh") else None  # M:SHELL-ONLY

mutations.name: untagged-block-run
mutations._mechanism: A block with no screen is executed anyway: an arbitrary published command runs at certification time.

mutations.name: comment-only-line-is-a-screen
mutations._mechanism: A bare `# expect 0` line with no command is screened.
mutations.find: continue  # M:COMMENT-ONLY: a comment-only line is not a statement
mutations.replace: pass  # M:COMMENT-ONLY: a comment-only line is not a statement

mutations.name: annotated-screen-dropped
mutations._mechanism: `# expect 0 (VACUOUS ...)` and `# expect 0, run ...` stop being screens.

mutations.name: worded-expectation-is-a-screen
mutations._mechanism: `# expect 4 methods x 2` becomes expect=4.

mutations.name: repeated-markers-read
mutations._mechanism: A screen inside a loop prints its markers twice; the first pair is read.

mutations.name: mangled-labelled-repeated
mutations._mechanism: Review N2: begin=0, end=1 is labelled as repeated markers.

mutations.name: empty-status-list-read-as-clean
mutations._mechanism: Review N1: an end marker with no PIPESTATUS reads as a clean pipeline.
mutations.find: if not statuses or any(not s.isdigit() or int(s) >= 2 for s in statuses):  # M:PIPESTATUS
mutations.replace: if any(not s.isdigit() or int(s) >= 2 for s in statuses):  # M:PIPESTATUS

mutations.name: pipeline-error-reads-as-zero
mutations._mechanism: A member that errored (grep on a missing file, exit 2) is ignored, so `| wc -l` prints 0 and the screen PASSES.
mutations.find: if not statuses or any(not s.isdigit() or int(s) >= 2 for s in statuses):  # M:PIPESTATUS

mutations.name: non-integer-not-refused
mutations._mechanism: Output that is not one integer is not refused before comparison.

mutations.name: value-not-compared
mutations._mechanism: Any readable integer PASSES regardless of N.
mutations.find: return value, "PASS" if int(value) == expect else "FAIL"  # M:COMPARE

mutations.name: unset-verdict-defaults-to-pass
mutations._mechanism: A screen whose block timed out keeps its default verdict, which now reads PASS.

mutations.name: earlier-failure-ignored
mutations._mechanism: Review M2: a recorded failure before the screen is not read; the screen PASSES on a broken preamble.

mutations.name: trap-never-armed
mutations._mechanism: Review M2: no ERR trap, so nothing before a screen is ever recorded.

mutations.name: failed-assignment-not-recorded
mutations._mechanism: Review M2: an assignment whose command substitution failed with status 1 is not recorded; `$B..HEAD` collapses and reads 0.

mutations.name: no-match-recorded-as-failure
mutations._mechanism: Review M2's threshold: grep's exit 1 (no match) before a screen poisons it.

mutations.name: error-status-not-recorded
mutations._mechanism: Review M2: an exit >= 2 before a screen is not recorded.

mutations.name: trap-armed-inside-screens
mutations._mechanism: The trap stays armed inside a screen; on bash 3.2 it clobbers PIPESTATUS and an erroring member before a no-match count reads 0.

mutations.name: trap-not-rearmed-after-a-screen
mutations._mechanism: After the first screen the trap is never re-armed, so a failure between screens is missed.

mutations.name: failure-line-misattributed
mutations._mechanism: The recorded line is off by one, so the reason names the wrong document line.

mutations.name: failure-reported-at-heredoc-terminator
mutations._mechanism: A failing heredoc command is reported at its terminator line (where bash's LINENO lands), not the line that runs it.
mutations.find: doc_line = lines_at[lexed[k].body if lexed[k].body is not None else k][0]  # M:ORIGIN-OPENER

mutations.name: ansi-c-quote-not-tracked
mutations._mechanism: Review R2-M1(b): `$'it\'s'` is read as a plain single quote, which never closes; every later screen is swallowed.

mutations.name: arithmetic-shift-is-a-heredoc
mutations._mechanism: Review R2-M1(c): `$((1<<n))` opens a heredoc named n; every later line becomes its body.
mutations.find: elif (text.startswith("<<", k) and not arith  # M:ARITH-NOT-HEREDOC

mutations.name: heredoc-found-inside-quotes
mutations._mechanism: Review R2-M1(a): `<<` is searched over the whole code span again, quoted text included, so `'<<EOF'` opens a heredoc.
mutations.replace:
info.op = info.code.rstrip().endswith(("|", "&&", "|&"))  # M:CONT-OP-CODE
            pending.extend((m.group(3), m.group(1) == "-", i) for m in HEREDOC.finditer(info.code) if "'" in info.code)

mutations.name: unparsed-screen-dropped
mutations._mechanism: Review R2-M1 fail-closed: a published `# expect` the lexer did not accept is dropped instead of counted UNREADABLE.

mutations.name: unparsed-only-reads-as-none
mutations._mechanism: Review R2-M1 fail-closed: a document whose only screen is unparsed reports NONE instead of FAIL.
mutations.find: if not any(spans or unparsed_in(texts, spans) for spans, texts in tagged):
mutations.replace: if not any(spans for spans, texts in tagged):

mutations.name: comment-after-semicolon-missed
mutations._mechanism: Review R2 nit: `echo 0;# expect 0` is a comment in bash, but only a `#` after a blank starts one here.
mutations.find: elif ch == "#" and (k == 0 or text[k - 1] in " \t;&|()<>"):  # M:COMMENT-UNQUOTED
mutations.replace: elif ch == "#" and (k == 0 or text[k - 1] in " \t"):  # M:COMMENT-UNQUOTED

mutations.name: no-errtrace
mutations._mechanism: Review R2-M2: without `set -E` the ERR trap does not fire in a function body; a failed assignment there reads PASS.
mutations.find: "set -E",  # M:ERRTRACE: the trap also fires inside function bodies
mutations.replace: "true",  # M:ERRTRACE: the trap also fires inside function bodies

mutations.name: grep-no-match-in-assignment-poisons
mutations._mechanism: Review R2-S1: `X=$(… | grep pat)` that matches nothing (status 1) is recorded as a failure.
mutations.find: case "$t" in grep*|egrep*|fgrep*) if [ "$r" = 1 ]; then k=0; fi;; esac;;  # M:GREP-NOMATCH

mutations.name: env-prefix-is-an-assignment
mutations._mechanism: Review R2-S1: `LC_ALL=C grep …` is classified as an assignment, so grep's no-match is recorded as a failure.

mutations.name: stdin-inherited
mutations._mechanism: Review S4: the block reads the caller's stdin, so a screen's reading depends on how the tool was invoked.

mutations.name: runs-outside-the-sha-worktree
mutations._mechanism: The block no longer changes into the throwaway worktree.

mutations.name: git-dir-inherited
mutations._mechanism: Review M5: an inherited GIT_DIR makes every screen read the caller's HEAD.

mutations.name: subdirectory-root-ignored
mutations._mechanism: A ROOT below its repository's top runs the screens at the worktree top.
mutations.find: screens = evaluate(blocks, os.path.join(wt, prefix.stdout.strip()), timeout, pidfile)

mutations.name: sha-not-checked-as-commit
mutations._mechanism: The commit-type check is skipped; a bad sha is caught only later, under another reason.

mutations.name: worktree-left-behind
mutations._mechanism: The throwaway worktree is not removed.

mutations.name: repo-wide-prune
mutations._mechanism: Review M4: cleanup prunes the whole repository, deleting a moved-away worktree's entry.

mutations.name: own-entry-not-deleted
mutations._mechanism: Review M4: when `worktree remove --force` refuses (the block locked its worktree), this run's own entry stays registered.

mutations.name: sigterm-skips-cleanup
mutations._mechanism: Review M3: SIGTERM keeps Python's default disposition; no `finally` runs and the worktree stays registered.

mutations.name: block-survives-termination
mutations._mechanism: Review M3: on SIGTERM the worktree is removed but the block's process group keeps running.

mutations.name: none-reads-as-pass
mutations._mechanism: No tagged screen prints `EXPECT: PASS screens=0` and exits 0.

mutations.name: unreadable-reads-as-pass
mutations._mechanism: Only mismatches fail the summary; an all-UNREADABLE run prints PASS.
